text:
Maria: Anyone else seeing telemetry silence in eu-west1? dashboards show gpu_util and kv_cache_hits dropping ~06:12 UTC and a spike in 429s on /v1/infer.
ops-bot: Alert: observability_missing(eu-west1): gpu_util, kv_cache_hits, otel_exporter_error — triggered 06:14 UTC
infra-oncall: I'm looking. Can someone grab otel/exporter pod logs and egress-proxy rules?
Devon: grabbing logs now. First pass shows exporters repeatedly failing to dial the collector. Logs: ```
2026-03-17T06:12:19Z error exporter/otlp: dial tcp 10.240.3.12:4317: connect: connection refused
2026-03-17T06:12:21Z warn exporter/retry: retrying batch, attempt=4
2026-03-17T06:12:28Z error exporter/otlp: failed to send spans: broken pipe
```
Shay: We rolled an egress-proxy change in eu-west1 at ~05:55 to lock down new NAT ranges. Could be blocking internal VIPs.
Alyssa: Confirmed — the new egress policy denies outbound to the collector VIP (10.240.3.12:4317) because it only whitelisted cloud egress ranges.
Maria: That explains the silent dashboards. No spans/metrics reaching telemetry -> everything looks like a service outage.
infra-oncall: Mitigation plan: 1) temporarily relax egress-proxy to allow collector VIP 10.240.3.12:4317, 2) restart otel-collector/exporter pods to flush backpressure, 3) run a metrics backfill for the gap.
Devon: Applying relax now: `kubectl apply -f egress-relax-eu1.yaml -n infra` — tailing exporter logs.
deploy-bot: deploy infra/egress-relax-eu1.yaml succeeded (rev 67) — 06:17 UTC
Devon: exporter logs now show successful dial/connect and processed batches: ```
2026-03-17T06:17:42Z info exporter/otlp: connected to 10.240.3.12:4317
2026-03-17T06:17:45Z info exporter/queue: processed batch size=96
```
ops-bot: Observability ingest recovered for eu-west1 — metrics and traces resumed (06:18 UTC)
Maria: Dashboards are repopulating but there's a gap 06:12–06:17. We should backfill kv_cache_hits and gpu_util for cost analysis and evals.
Shay: Quick win: add a lightweight synthetic `kv_cache_unavailable` gauge emitted by runtime when local cache trips so next time we can alert before exporters fill. I'll open a PR.
Alyssa: Also propose a pushgateway in eu-west1 for services that buffer metrics locally — allow them to push backfilled samples when connectivity restores.
infra-oncall: Incident ticket created: incident/infra#523. Action items: rollback risky egress rules, add kv_cache_unavailable metric + alert, deploy pushgateway backfill path, add exporter_retry metrics. Assigning to @Shay and @Devon.
Devon: Backfill approach — run a one-off job that reads buffered metrics and uses remote_write. Example remote_write snippet: ```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: https://prom-remote.eu-west1.redwood/api/v1/write
    basic_auth:
      username: _token
      password: <redacted>
    send_exemplars: true
```
Maria: Noted: during the failover we shifted traffic to us-west1 which kept latency within SLOs but bumped GPU spend ~12% for the 30m window. Finance tag: COST-INCIDENT-1870001111.
Shay: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/918 — adds `kv_cache_unavailable` gauge + alert (5m burn).
Devon: Backfill job completed and Prometheus shows kv_cache_hits/gpu_util filling the gap. Marked window in observability UI so evals ignore it.
infra-oncall: Post-incident items: revert/authorize egress changes (network owners), add egress integration tests for collector IPs, runtime telemetry for local buffering (`buffered_metric_count`), cost runbook for cross-region surge.
ops-bot: Incident resolved — mitigation complete (06:40 UTC).
Maria: Thanks all. Keeping follow-ups in incident/infra#523 — ping infra-oncall if it recurs.
